nodes.description: The unifying mechanism across SHFM loci is failure to maintain normal apical ectodermal ridge (AER) function during limb development. The AER is the epithelial signaling center at the distal tip of the limb bud that sustains outgrowth of the underlying mesenchyme. SHFM-associated mutations converge on dysregulation of FGF8 in the central portion of the AER, failure of AER stratification, and disruption of reciprocal Wnt-BMP-FGF signaling between the AER and progress-zone mesenchyme. The central-ray defect reflects loss of this signaling specifically in the median AER.

nodes.description: The family 2 deletion reported by Lango Allen et al. removes the DYNC1I1 exon 15- and exon 17-associated limb enhancers together with additional DYNC1I1 and SLC25A13 exons. DLX5 and DLX6 remain disomic. The physical loss includes protein-coding sequence, but the proposed limb mechanism is loss of regulation of the intact DLX5/DLX6 genes. DYNC1I1 and SLC25A13 are annotated here for sequence overlap, without attributing all effects of the multigene deletion to either protein.

nodes.description: Loss of central-AER FGF8 dysregulates the reciprocal Wnt-BMP-FGF signaling loop. nodes.description: Loss of the DYNC1I1 exonic enhancer region is proposed to impair DLX5/DLX6 expression during limb development. Human enhancer fragments drive limb reporters in mice, and the endogenous mouse exon 15-associated region contacts Dlx5/Dlx6 promoters in the E11.5 apical ectodermal ridge. These experiments support enhancer function and candidate targets; they do not measure the expression change in the human deletion carriers. DYNC1I1 is the enhancer host and is not itself expressed in the assayed mouse embryonic limb.

nodes.description: Family 2 in Lango Allen et al. carries the breakpoint-sequenced deletion NC_000007.13:g.95704812_95810747del, reported as 105,935 bp on the GRCh37 chromosome 7 reference. It partially removes DYNC1I1 exons 14-17 and SLC25A13 exons 11-18, including the two named limb enhancers, while leaving DLX5 and DLX6 disomic. The proband and his maternal uncle had isolated SHFM with differing numbers of affected limbs; unaffected carriers demonstrate incomplete penetrance. DLX6 is a co-target of the deleted enhancer region alongside DLX5. This particular allele's coordinates are not universal boundaries for SHFM1 regulatory variants.
